chapter: Properties of matter: elasticity, viscosity, surface tension

variants.title: Optical lever: Young's modulus of a steel wire
variants.note: Steel is the stiffest of the three wires: 1 kg stretches it by only 0.2 mm.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals; BS 3737 standard wire gauge: steel about 200 GPa, SWG 24 = 0.559 mm (from memory - verify)

variants.title: Optical lever: Young's modulus of a brass wire
variants.note: Brass is about half as stiff as steel.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals; BS 3737 standard wire gauge: brass about 100 GPa, SWG 22 = 0.711 mm (from memory - verify)

variants.title: Optical lever: Young's modulus of a copper wire
variants.note: Copper is a little stiffer than brass; keep the load small so it stays elastic.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals; BS 3737 standard wire gauge: copper about 110 GPa, SWG 22 = 0.711 mm (from memory - verify)
